_: Kill-check for the skip rule and the related-tests cut (`asc-09wx.14`, cuts 1 and 3), the two halves of `scripts/gate-scope.mjs` and the one seam it opens into `vitest.test-count.ts` and `scripts/gate.mjs`. The direction that matters here is the one that FAILS OPEN: a rule that decides a commit cannot reach a test, and is wrong, produces a green verdict nobody earned -- `dogfood/0061`'s shape, and the reason this repo treats a false green as the worst class of defect. So most mutants push the rule toward SKIPPING (M1 unmapped entries, M2 the whole `.ascend` tree, M7 an empty staged set, M8 all of `packages/`) rather than toward running too much, which is merely expensive. The other four are the cut's two ends: M3 and M4 remove the closure and the cross-package scanners from the reachable set, so a change stops running the tests that read it; M5 and M6 are the interaction the plan had to settle before the cut could exist at all -- a subset run that overwrites `.testcount/scan.json` makes `scripts/test-baseline.mjs` report a breach on EVERY commit, a false red blamed on the tests rather than on the cut. M9 through M12 sit in `scripts/gate.mjs` and cover the wire: the scope variable that has to arrive at the reporter, the skip that has to be recorded rather than left absent, the step list that has to actually be narrowed, and -- M12, added after the end-to-end drive found it -- the full run having to SAY it is full rather than letting the reporter infer it from a variable it inherited. M5 and M6 are deliberately a pair -- M5 breaks the predicate, M6 removes the reporter's use of it -- because a guard that is asserted and a guard that is unwired are the same green, and only the second mutant distinguishes them. The killers were found empirically rather than guessed: each mutant was applied, the owning files were run with vitest's JSON reporter, and the failing test names were read off its assertionResults. Every mutant below was killed; there are no intended survivors.
